intended: All four classes are Year 4 groups at Ashcombe Primary in one autumn term taught by Vance, so the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before. The scope clause beside that fact has every logged class taking its English lessons as one whole group, so every lesson was delivered to half as many pupils as in the term the class is measured against. Each class is compared against itself in the previous autumn term, when the groups were twice the size, so the evidence cannot separate the smaller classes from the reading program. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the scores covering every pupil on roll, so no second defect is present.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every class: "Class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group." Halved class size applies to the very English lessons being scored, so it explains the 5-9 point comprehension gain over the previous autumn term independently of the reading program.

reported: The confounder reaches the units: "Class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group." Because English was taught to the whole class, the halved roll halved the group size in the very lessons being measured, so smaller classes explain the 5-9 point comprehension gain over the previous autumn term.

intended: In cases one and three the extra running hours were recorded before the redesigned bearing was fitted: the lathe reading is dated 27 March but the bearing went in on 4 May, and the conveyor reading is dated 21 July but the bearing went in on 2 August. Half the evidence therefore describes service life already accumulated at the time of fitting, so it cannot bear on the redesign at all. That leaves cases two and four, which are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four cases have measurement endpoints that precede the fitting date: the lathe was 'fitted 4 May' but its result is reported 'by 27 March', and the conveyor was 'fitted 2 August' with its result 'by 21 July'. The other two cases run ~6-7 weeks forward (9 January to 24 February; 6 October to 25 November), so cases one and three are dated backwards and cannot record post-fitting service life.

reported: Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the bearing was fitted: case One was 'fitted 4 May' but its extra 340 hours are counted 'by 27 March', and case Three was 'fitted 2 August' but counted 'by 21 July'. The two well-ordered cases (9 January to 24 February, 6 October to 25 November) run about six weeks, so the reversed pairs cannot be read as spanning into the following year.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and the clause beside it records that about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed. The claim is about the germination of the coated lot, so the population is every tray sown from it and the germination points describe four fifths of that. Seed that takes a full coat is the plump, well-filled grain, while the light and cracked seed comes off the coater thinly covered, so a rate built on the fully coated trays alone sits above the lot's own rate, and the 9, 6, 11 and 7 point gains are consistent with each lot's germination being unchanged. All four lots are fescue at Hollin Bank in one spring under grower Marek, so the same missing fifth sits under every case.
reported: The germination figures are restricted to a favourable subset: "Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed" - so roughly 20 percent of each lot's trays are excluded from the post-coating scores while the previous spring sowing is scored whole. The 6-11 point gains therefore describe a narrower population than the lots the claim is about.

reported: The germination rates "cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat" while "about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed" and are excluded, so the 9/6/11/7 point gains rest on seed selected for having taken a full coat. Seed that takes a full coat is plausibly the plumper, sounder seed, so the excluded fifth makes the measured population narrower than the lot the claim is about.

intended: In cases one and three the fledgling count was recorded before the boxes went up: 27 March precedes 3 June at Hollowmere, and 24 September precedes 2 November at Brackenfen. Half the evidence therefore describes young that had already fledged when the boxes were installed, so it cannot be evidence for the boxes. The two remaining cases, Cransley and Vanehead, are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four cases have outcome dates that precede the intervention: plot One was "boxed 3 June" but fledging is counted "by 27 March", and plot Three was "boxed 2 November" but counted "by 24 September". The boxes cannot have raised counts measured months before they were installed, and the seasons quoted (spring, autumn) do not match the installation dates either.
